applied.message: $or of equalities on one field (region) is an $in: one index scan with point bounds instead of a subplan per branch, and sort-compatible.
total: $gte and $lte carry the same value, which is an equality the planner treats as a range (breaks ESR key order and invites near-tied plans). Rewrite to an equality.
countDocuments({}) scans the collection or the _id index. For a whole-collection total use estimatedDocumentCount(), which reads collection metadata.

findings.message: Separate predicates on attrs.k and attrs.v can be satisfied by different elements of the attrs array, so an element k=a,v=1 next to k=b,v=2 matches k=a,v=2. Put both inside { attrs: { $elemMatch: { k: …, v: … } } } and index { "attrs.k": 1, "attrs.v": 1 }. Reported, not applied: it changes the result set.
qty $gte "10" compares strings lexicographically ("10" < "2"). If the field holds numbers as strings, results are wrong; store numbers as numbers. Reported, not applied.
$push: "$$ROOT" carries whole documents into $group memory (100 MB per stage). $project only the fields you need first.
docs builds an unbounded array with $push and a later stage slices it. Use a bounded accumulator ($firstN / $lastN / $topN / $bottomN, 5.2+) so the discarded elements are never held in memory.
$where runs JavaScript per document, cannot use an index, and is deprecated from 8.0. Rewrite with native query operators or $expr.

skip(5000) walks and discards 5000 index keys or documents on every page, and on a sharded collection mongos asks each shard for limit+skip. Use keyset pagination: sort on a unique key and filter { _id: { $gt: lastSeenId } } with limit().
batchSize(2) multiplies getMore round-trips; on a change stream each getMore re-scans the oplog window. Use the default (101 first batch, then up to 16 MiB) or a larger value.

status: $ne cannot use selective index bounds and also matches documents missing the field. Where the domain is known, match the wanted values positively ($in / equality) — this changes results unless the field is always present, so it is not auto-applied.
/smith/ is not anchored, so it scans every index key (or document). Anchor it with ^ if the value is a prefix, or use Atlas Search for substring / full-text matching.
sort() without limit(): if no index supplies this order, the whole result is sorted in memory (100 MB blocking-sort cap; spills or fails). Back the sort with an index or add a limit.

Rewritten query:
// Run: mdbx optimize examples/slow-queries.mql
// Each query below carries a common performance defect the static MQL optimizer catches.
use shop

// 1. Negation, unanchored case-insensitive regex, same-field $or, degenerate range,
//    deep skip paging and a tiny batch size — in one find().
db.orders.find({
  status: { $ne: "cancelled" },
  name: /smith/i,
  region: { $in: ["EU", "US"] },
  total: 100
}).sort({ createdAt: -1 }).skip(5000).batchSize(2)

// 2. A healthy query: the optimizer only recommends the ESR index that also covers the projection.
db.orders.find(
  { customerId: 42, createdAt: { $gt: ISODate("2026-01-01") } },
  { customerId: 1, total: 1, createdAt: 1 }
).sort({ total: -1 }).limit(20)

// 3. Pipeline: $match buried after transparent stages, key/value attributes without $elemMatch,
//    $push of whole documents then $slice, and an unindexed $lookup.
db.events.aggregate([
  { $match: { tenant: "t1", "attrs.k": "color", "attrs.v": "red" } },
  { $addFields: { day: { $dateTrunc: { date: "$ts", unit: "day" } } } },
  { $sort: { ts: -1 } },
  { $group: { _id: "$day", docs: { $push: "$$ROOT" } } },
  { $project: { top: { $slice: ["$docs", 5] } } },
  { $lookup: { from: "users", localField: "uid", foreignField: "userId", as: "u" } }
])

// 4. Counting everything with a filter-based count.
db.orders.estimatedDocumentCount()

// 5. JavaScript predicate and a numeric value compared as a string.
db.inventory.find({ $where: "this.qty > this.reorderLevel", qty: { $gte: "10" } })
